item.title: Major zircon deposit found in Xinjiang
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Major zircon deposit found in Xinjiang Discovery follows nearly two decades of sustained efforts to secure key mineral China has made a breakthrough in its mineral exploration efforts after a major zircon sand deposit was discovered in Baicheng county, Aksu prefecture, Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region. The Ministry of Natural Resources announced the discovery, with confirmed resources equivalent to those of more than 40 large zircon deposits and associated hafnium resources reaching a super-large scale, at a news conference in Beijing on Saturday. The discovery marks a major breakthrough in China's efforts to secure supplies of zircon, a mineral of which the country has relatively scarce resources. Around 70 percent of the world's zircon reserves are concentrated in Australia, while China accounts for less than 1 percent. The new find is expected to significantly strengthen the country's resource security. Zirconium, a silvery-gray transition metal, has a high melting point, excellent corrosion resistance and a low neutron absorption cross-section. These properties make it an important material for nuclear reactor fuel rod cladding and high-temperature alloys used in aerospace applications. Hafnium, which is commonly found alongside zirconium, has a high density and melting point. It is used in nuclear reactor control rods, rocket engines and spacecraft heat shields. Zhu Yilin, chief engineer of the Xinjiang department of natural resources, said the discovery was the culmination of nearly two decades of sustained exploration. Between 2006 and 2019, geologists reanalyzed historical geochemical survey data from the Tianshan region, and identified multiple zircon anomalies and promising exploration targets. According to Zhu, the regional government has allocated 35.19 million yuan ($5.28 million) to five zircon exploration projects since 2024, which led to the breakthrough following extensive fieldwork. "We will intensify exploration in promising zircon belts in Aksu, expand project deployment, strengthen metallogenic research and improve exploration technologies, with the aim of achieving further breakthroughs," Zhu said. He added that efforts would also be made to accelerate the transfer of mining rights through public bidding, encouraging rights holders to expand reserves and increase production. The discovery is among the major achievements of China's latest round of mineral exploration in the inaugural year of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-30). Other significant discoveries have also been made across the country. The discovery of a major copper-gold deposit in the Chating region of Xuancheng, Anhui province, was announced by the Ministry of Natural Resources in September. The exploration project completed nearly 100,000 meters of drilling in just four months. Meanwhile, Guizhou province reported the discovery of its first fully concealed, high-grade, thick and super-large lead-zinc deposit in Bijie. To gain a more comprehensive understanding of the country's mineral resources and strengthen resource security, the ministry has also launched a new round of resource reassessment during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, targeting associated and low-grade minerals, as well as strategic mineral resources that were previously difficult to exploit but may now be economically recoverable with advances in technology. limenghan@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Draft standard aiming to speed C-V2X rollout
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Draft standard aiming to speed C-V2X rollout A proposed mandatory national standard requiring commercial road transport in China to be fitted with cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) systems could accelerate the technology's rollout beyond pilot projects. The Ministry of Transport released the draft for public comment earlier this year. It is now under review after the comment period ended on Aug 29. Under the proposal, vehicles used in commercial road transport, other than trailers, would have to be equipped with systems using LTEV2X, a 4G-based form of C-V2X. The technology enables vehicles to exchange safety information directly with nearby vehicles and roadside infrastructure, supporting warnings about potential collisions and other road hazards. If adopted, the provision would turn C-V2X installation from a voluntary practice into a regulatory requirement for covered vehicles. Fan Ju, deputy general manager of CICT Connected and Intelligent Technologies, said C-V2X can warn drivers of hazards including rear-end collision risks, collision risks involving vehicles hidden from view by obstacles, and accidents ahead. Such functions can complement onboard cameras and radar, giving drivers or driver-assistance systems more time to respond, he said. Fan said the cost of installing C-V2X equipment during vehicle production is now relatively low. However, some automakers remain reluctant to adopt the technology because consumers may not perceive its benefits as readily as more visible features such as large infotainment screens. Deliveries of passenger vehicles fitted with C-V2X as standard equipment in China reached 344,000 in the first half, up 13.63 percent year-on-year, according to data from research institute Gaogong. In addition, C-V2X penetration in the passenger vehicle market stood at 4.03 percent. The proposal comes as China advances a vehicle-road-cloud integration pilot program launched by five government departments in 2024. The program covers 20 pilot areas, requires all participating vehicles to be equipped with C-V2X terminals and sets a 50 percent installation target for new vehicles in those areas. The pilot framework also calls for full 5G coverage in the pilot areas, connectivity for at least 90 percent of traffic signals and road signs, and LTE-V2X roadside communication units. Roadside sensing and edge-computing systems are to be deployed at key intersections and road sections. Figures published by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology in late 2025 put the number of intelligent roadside units deployed nationwide at more than 11,000. Automakers including FAW, SAIC, BYD and Nio have also launched production models equipped with C-V2X as standard. During the 2026 World Intelligent Connected Vehicles Conference in Beijing, vehicles from several automakers took part in a demonstration in which roadside sensors and communication networks alerted drivers and driver-assistance systems to pedestrians and cyclists obscured from view. Li Keqiang, an academician with the Chinese Academy of Engineering, said that 22 Chinese and foreign companies were taking part in a joint initiative to advance vehicle-road-cloud integration, up from 15 in 2025. The initiative also covered the development and testing of related functions on 21 models. Li said broader commercial cooperation is also taking shape, with 14 partnerships involving 26 companies across the automotive value chain, including automakers, companies involved in city-level vehicle networks and connected-vehicle component suppliers. He expects initial vehicle-road-cloud functions to be introduced in production vehicles by the end of 2026 and more closely integrated with driver-assistance systems in 2027. wangyuchen@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero makes a heroic debut
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Following the phenomenal appearance of Black Myth: Wukong in 2024, the world recently witnessed the launch of another AAA-rated video game, Phantom Blade Zero, developed by a Chinese gaming company. Less than an hour after its release on Thursday, the game, developed by S-Game, had surpassed 300,000 concurrent players on Steam, a digital distribution platform for PC games, with the player count climbing to more than 720,000 at its peak later that day. In pre-release reviews, the PC version of Phantom Blade Zero earned an average score of 88 on the US review aggregator website Metacritic, surpassing the 81 scored by Black Myth: Wukong. On Steam, 88 percent of more than 33,250 Chinese-language users gave positive reviews, while the figure among English-language users also reached 88 percent. So far, the game has sold over 1 million copies, with preorder sales on the Steam and PS5 platforms estimated to surpass $43 million. US video game critic Travis Northup rated it 9 out of 10, praising the action role-playing game as "amazing". In his review on the US entertainment media platform Imagine Games Network, Northup wrote: "Phantom Blade Zero is an unbelievably smooth action game filled with memorable boss fights, compelling combat, and limitless swagger. … It is one of the best action games I've played in a long time." He added that "its tale of betrayal and revenge mostly plays it extremely safe, and some unfortunate invisible barriers and technical hiccups can cause minor frustrations — but the overwhelming majority of my time with this stunning, incredibly well-tuned adventure was downright awesome". The game begins with the story of a highly skilled martial artist named Soul, whose heart has been severely injured in a previous battle. On the verge of death, he is saved by a mysterious doctor. However, the treatment leaves him with only 66 days to live before his heart will ultimately fail. In the last days of his life, Soul embarks on a journey to find a new heart and to rediscover his true self and his original sense of chivalry in this dark phantom world full of lies and betrayals. It "truly captures the essence of the martial arts world in (prestigious Chinese writer) Gu Long's novels, which is dark, chaotic, brutal, and romantic", said Feng Ji, the producer of Black Myth: Wukong, in his WeChat Moments after watching the livestreaming of an actual gameplay preview in July. Before its official release, some 3 million people across all platforms added Phantom Blade Zero to their wish lists, making it one of the most anticipated Chinese action games of 2026. One of the reasons behind the game's popularity among foreign players lies in its rich kung fu elements. Liang Qiwei, or Soulframe Liang, founder of S-Game and the game's producer, said, "At its core, it's a story rich with traditional Chinese elements". Liang, 45, made his first game at Tsinghua University 21 years ago. In actual gameplay, what particularly impresses global players is the smooth, refreshing combat design in a style concept called "kungfupunk". "Kungfupunk" blends traditional elements of Chinese wuxia (a fiction genre centered on martial arts adventures in ancient China), an atmosphere of ancient jianghu, or the realm of martial arts, steampunk-style machinery, occult body modification, and a dark, rebellious punk spirit to create a new form of expression, Liang told media in an earlier interview. In this world, swordsmen, martial arts sects and old Chinese architecture coexist with mechanical limbs, grim industrial ruins and modern rock music. "We are creating an original global IP that belongs to us, strongly imprinted with the essence of Chinese wuxia culture," Liang said. The game offers a total of 30 different weapons, all inspired by the vast collection of traditional Chinese weaponry. "To understand how the weight and length of these weapons affect movement, we sometimes invite swordsmiths to forge them," Liang said in an article published online in April. The martial arts moves are captured from more than 20 highly experienced kung fu actors, including Hong Kong movie star Donnie Yen. Additionally, the production team explored locations like ancestral halls in Fujian province, ancient towns in Zhejiang province, and Beijing's old steel factories, scanning and creatively combining them into the unique "kungfupunk" art style.

item.title: South-South cooperation boon to world economy
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
South-South cooperation boon to world economy The foundations for cooperation across countries and regions of the Global South are expanding. According to the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development, South-South merchandise exports rose from approximately $500 billion in 1995 to $6.8 trillion in 2025. More than half of developing countries' exports now go to other developing economies. At the same time, countries still differ significantly in their development conditions, industrial structures and ability to withstand external shocks. The key question is how to strengthen the development resilience of the Global South, or, how to translate its potential for cooperation into the capacity to drive shared development. The answers lie in the following areas. Respond to external shocks In the face of unilateralism and protectionism, the Global South should strengthen coordination and firmly uphold the multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core. We should safeguard basic principles such as most-favored-nation treatment and ensure that reforms respond more fully to the concerns of developing members. For small and medium-sized economies, predictable and nondiscriminatory rules are essential for businesses to gain fair access to international markets. Cooperation must respond to the practical needs of businesses. In my view, we can give priority to facilitating customs clearance, improving logistics connectivity and sharing market information. These efforts can help businesses find more trading partners and diversify their sources of supply. For essential products such as food and energy — which affect people's livelihoods — we should strengthen policy communication and reduce the impact of sudden policy changes on partner countries. A UN survey covering 174 economies in 2025 found that the global implementation rate for paperless trade measures was 72 percent, while the rate for cross-border paperless trade measures was 49 percent. When a trading partner accepts an electronic certificate of origin, a small or medium-sized business may save an administrative step and several days of waiting. Such practical improvements can gradually reduce the costs of doing business and boost overall trade. The Global South can begin with pilot projects at ports of entry and in sectors where conditions are suitable, expand their coverage as experience is gained and use technical assistance to help partners with more limited capacity participate. South-South cooperation should remain open and inclusive, with South-South and North-South cooperation reinforcing one another. By working with more partners and keeping trading channels open, countries can strengthen their ability to respond to external uncertainties and bring greater stability to the world economy. Improve industrial capabilities Shifts in industrial and supply chains have created opportunities for some countries in the Global South to attract investment and develop manufacturing. Once projects are in place, the sustainability of cooperation depends in part on how they generate local employment, develop skills and support local businesses. Openness to trade and investment and the development of local industries need to be supported by complementary policies. When attracting investment, countries can also improve power supplies and logistics, provide vocational training, and help local small and medium-sized enterprises meet quality and delivery standards. Local businesses can then gradually enter supply chains and share in the opportunities created by investment cooperation. The China-Egypt TEDA Suez Economic and Trade Cooperation Zone offers a practical example. By end-2025, the zone had attracted nearly 200 enterprises and more than $3.8 billion in actual investment, directly creating around 10,000 local jobs. High-voltage electrical equipment is manufactured locally in the zone, and products such as glass fiber are sold in international markets. The zone demonstrates how industrial cooperation can create a positive link between cross-border investment and stronger local manufacturing capabilities. Every country has a legitimate interest in developing its own industries. Industrial policy should reflect national conditions, respect multilateral rules, and emphasize transparency and effective implementation. Industries at an early stage of development can receive appropriate support within the limits allowed by established rules. Such support should be accompanied by mechanisms for evaluation and adjustment, with more resources directed toward infrastructure, technological research and development, and workers' skills. Cooperation projects should also fully respect host countries' development plans and take into account environmental protection, workers' interests and the interests of local communities. Cooperation has a sound foundation when businesses are willing to invest for the long term and local communities receive tangible benefits. Furthermore, equipment needs people to maintain it once it is in use, and production lines need people to manage them once they are built. Universities, vocational colleges and businesses can jointly develop training programs so that industrial cooperation and talent development advance together. Ultimately, industrial development should strengthen local capabilities. Enhance financial cooperation Financial market volatility affects trade and investment through exchange rates, interest rates and capital flows. In strengthening financial cooperation, the Global South should focus on real trade and project needs and improve arrangements for settlement, financing and risk management. For trade settlement, countries can steadily expand the use of local currencies in line with market demand and businesses' voluntary participation, while improving direct currency conversion, clearing and supporting financing services. In 2025, the central banks of Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand harmonized and broadened the operational rules of the Local Currency Transaction Framework, providing a more coordinated framework for cross-border trade and investment. This experience merits study in light of each country's circumstances. Local currency settlement can reduce some of the costs of converting through an intermediate currency. Better matching the currencies in which businesses receive income and make payments can also help them manage exchange rate risks. Exchange rates between currencies still fluctuate, and the actual benefits depend on market liquidity, financing costs and the availability of hedging tools. We should therefore give businesses greater convenience and choice, backed by appropriate financial services. For long-term investment, multilateral development institutions such as the Shanghai-based New Development Bank can help expand local currency financing and co-financing. In 2023, the NDB issued its first bonds in South Africa, totaling 1.5 billion rand ($90.25 million). It announced that the proceeds would be used for infrastructure and sustainable development projects in South Africa. This offers a practical way to raise funds in local capital markets and support local development. For projects that earn most of their revenue in local currency, appropriate use of local currency financing can reduce the risks arising from a mismatch between the currencies of revenue and debt service. Project cash flows, debt servicing capacity, and construction and operating conditions must also be assessed, with loan maturities set accordingly. Sound projects are the basis for lasting financial cooperation. Countries can also strengthen communication among central banks and regulatory authorities and improve currency swap, liquidity support and risk information-sharing arrangements suited to their circumstances. Regional cooperation should complement the global financial safety net, helping businesses that are operating normally continue their trade and investment activities during periods of market volatility. By making trade flows smoother, ensuring that industrial cooperation strengthens local capabilities and aligning financing more closely with the needs of the real economy, we can gradually improve our collective ability to respond to external shocks. We can also contribute to a fairer, more open and inclusive international economic order. The writer is a professor of the University of International Business and Economics. The views do not necessarily reflect those of China Daily.

item.title: Carrying lingka spirit into autumn chill
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Carrying lingka spirit into autumn chill A seasonal pastime remains a social fixture as new venues extend the tradition into colder months, Palden Nyima and Zheng Jinran report. A light autumn rain fell over a mountain valley on the northern outskirts of Lhasa, capital of the Xizang autonomous region. Inside the glass-walled rooms at A-Tso Manor, families and friends gathered around tables, sipping tea and coffee, sharing meals and enjoying a leisurely weekend. Outside, children played in the courtyard as the smell of grilled meat drifted from a barbecue area. Clouds partly obscured the surrounding mountains, and the September air carried a distinct chill. Yet inside the heated rooms, the gatherings continued in warmth and comfort. The scene captures how guo lingka, a long-standing Tibetan tradition of spending leisure time outdoors with family and friends, is finding new expressions beyond its customary summer season. Grassy riverbanks and colorful tents remain hallmarks of summer outings. But venues offering heated indoor spaces, ready-made meals and modern recreational facilities are making the pastime possible throughout the year. Dudul, manager of A-Tso Manor, said the venue combines outdoor recreation with year-round dining and leisure services that cater to visitors in every season. "In summer, many guests prefer sitting outside on the grass, enjoying the sunshine and fresh air," Dudul says. "When the weather gets colder, they can move indoors, where heating keeps them comfortable." The manor serves Chinese and Western dishes, along with coffee and other beverages. Guests can choose between outdoor canopies and indoor dining rooms without bringing their own cooking equipment, tents or food. For Metok, a Lhasa resident who enjoys weekend outings with relatives and friends, these changes have turned what was once a carefully planned excursion into a more spontaneous affair. "We used to bring everything ourselves, including meat, vegetables, gas cylinders, cooking utensils, tents and mats," she recalls. "Now we can simply come to a lingka venue and order whatever we want to eat." Metok remembers a time when meals on such outings consisted mainly of beef, potatoes and flour-based dishes. Today, the options are far more varied, while activities at some venues extend from traditional singing and dancing to swimming, games and other recreational pursuits. For older residents, the changes also bring back memories of how the tradition has evolved over generations. Konchok, 58, first experienced lingka outings as a young man in his 20s, when leisure destinations were concentrated around the city's established gardens and parks. "In those days, people mainly went to Norbulingka and the areas around Dzongyab Lukhang Park," he says. "Later, more people began visiting valleys around Lhasa, including Palding, Nyangral, and Dogde." The growing choice of destinations has brought greater convenience and improved facilities. Tents now come in a variety of sizes and styles, often furnished with tables, seating and entertainment equipment. Konchok says he and his friends went on lingka outings less frequently when they were young. Today, better facilities make it easier to arrange gatherings whenever time permits. The Tibetan word lingka means garden or park, while guo lingka refers to the practice of spending leisure time in natural surroundings, often eating, drinking tea, singing, dancing and socializing. Nyiten, an ethnology professor at Xizang University, says the custom has long been intertwined with local festivals and social traditions. Although historical records offer relatively few detailed accounts of this everyday pastime, lingka gatherings have been closely associated with the Shoton Festival. During the festival, residents traditionally enjoy yogurt, watch Tibetan opera and spend time together in gardens. The tradition also has links to gardens once used by Tibetan aristocratic families, and numerous place names containing the word lingka have survived in Lhasa.

item.title: Site in Beijing yields new evidence of Sui Great Wall
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Archaeologists have discovered remnants of a Sui Dynasty (581-618) section of the Great Wall in Beijing for the first time, providing fresh insights into the ancient fortification's development in northern China and the region's early military defense system. The discovery was announced at the Fourth Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei Archaeological Academic Exchange, held in Beijing on Saturday. The discovery was made during an excavation at the Dalinggou site, an early-stage Great Wall military outpost in Changping district. The excavations, conducted by the Beijing Institute of Archaeology from August to October, covered an area of 800 square meters. Archaeologists unearthed more than 60 ceramic and metal artifacts, including architectural components, items of daily use and weapons, dating to three historical periods: the Northern Qi Dynasty (550-577), the Sui Dynasty and the Jin Dynasty (1115-1234). According to Shang Heng from the Beijing Institute of Archaeology, the project's lead archaeologist, the site was previously identified as part of the Northern Qi Great Wall following a nationwide survey. However, archaeological evidence has now established that it was also in use during the Sui Dynasty. The conclusion is supported by discoveries of a Sui Dynasty wuzhu coin and a piece of porcelain displaying characteristics typical of the period. The wuzhu coin was a standard bronze cash coin in ancient China, famous for being the longest-circulating currency in Chinese history. Geographical evidence further supports the finding. The Dalinggou site lies along the same defensive line as several previously identified Sui Dynasty Great Wall remains in neighboring provinces. To the west, a stone inscription recording the construction of the Great Wall in the year 599 was found in Kelan county, Shanxi province. To the east, another inscription dating to 597 was found in Luanping county, Hebei province. A Sui Dynasty beacon tower has also been identified in Qianxi county, Hebei. The Sui Dynasty was a short-lived but pivotal dynasty in Chinese history. It ended political division by reunifying China in 589 and laid the foundation for the Tang Dynasty (618-907).

item.title: Deliveryman chases his poetic dream
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Deliveryman chases his poetic dream Share - WeChat
Born in 1969 in East China's Jiangsu province, Wang Jibing dropped out of school during junior high. To make a living, he worked as a construction worker, a sand dredger, a street vendor and a scrap collector. Yet, he never lost his appetite for reading, often lingering at secondhand book stalls and sifting through discarded newspapers. Life was hard, yet his love for literature never faded. "Literature is a candy in my life," he said. "I've never found that writing is mentally challenging. Passion is all that drives me."

item.title: CIIE sets stage for frontier technology
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
CIIE sets stage for frontier technology Exhibition to debut record of innovations as vast Chinese market beckons From discarded tires to rice husks, materials once considered waste are finding new uses in the automotive industry, as French tire and mobility company Michelin Group prepares to showcase a tire made with 75 percent renewable and recycled materials at the ninth China International Import Expo in Shanghai later this week. Set to make its Asian debut at the expo, the tire incorporates recovered carbon black, bio-based synthetic rubber, silica derived from rice husks and recycled steel, reflecting the growing use of alternative materials in automotive manufacturing. Ye Fei, president and CEO of Michelin China and Mongolia, said the CIIE offers an important platform for the company to introduce global innovations, respond to evolving demand in China and deepen cooperation with local industrial partners. The French company will also introduce its Touch Intelligence technology in Asia for the first time, reflecting the company's efforts to expand the use of digital technologies in tire monitoring and maintenance. Having participated in every edition of the CIIE, United States-based industrial group 3M will showcase its latest technologies and products in automotive, electronics and safety, as well as manufacturing materials and automation, with several products set to make their global or China debuts. "We have always viewed the CIIE as a key trade fair for showcasing cutting-edge innovations and expanding local partnerships," said Henry Ding, president of 3M China, adding that the company will further strengthen its supply chain network in China.

item.title: Self-governance of Party seen as strategic task
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
Self-governance of Party seen as strategic task Task: Strict management of officials seen as crucial Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, has emphasized the need to persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance to maintain the Party's advanced nature and integrity, consolidate its long-term governing position and provide strong guarantees for building China into a great modern socialist country in all respects and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation on all fronts through Chinese modernization. The remarks were made in Xi's explanation of a draft resolution on certain major issues concerning persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, and were delivered at the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, which concluded last week in Beijing. Both the explanation and the resolution, adopted at the plenum, were made public on Sunday. Explaining the choice of the plenum's agenda, Xi said that the CPC Central Committee made this major decision based on its assessment and thorough consideration of the situation and in light of the historical stage that the cause of the Party and the country has entered and the advancement of Chinese modernization as a whole. Xi said full and rigorous Party self-governance is a long-term strategic task, noting that problems and hidden dangers threaten to undermine the Party's advanced nature, weaken its integrity and jeopardize its long-term governance. He also stressed the need to consolidate and develop the sound political situation in which great solidarity and unity are maintained across the whole Party, and great cohesion is secured within the Party and the military and among the people. In the face of complicated international and domestic landscapes, Xi said that persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance is essential for fulfilling the Party's historic mission and ensuring steady and sustained progress in the cause of the Party and the country. A document drafting group headed by Xi was established by the CPC Central Committee in January this year and held its first general meeting on Feb 6, officially starting the drafting work. Xi said the CPC Central Committee promoted full democratic engagement, conducted thorough surveys and studies, and sought extensive input during drafting. On Jan 31, the CPC Central Committee issued a notice soliciting opinions from localities and departments on the plenum's topic and entrusted 16 organizations to research 23 major issues. Xi presided over a symposium in Shanghai on May 6 to hear opinions from principal leaders of some provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the central government. On Aug 3, a draft resolution was issued to certain Party members for feedback, including retired senior Party officials. Dedicated meetings were also held to solicit views from the central committees of other political parties in China, leaders of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce, and prominent figures without party affiliation. The Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee met three times and the Political Bureau met twice to review and revise the draft before its submission to the plenum. In addition to an opening paragraph and conclusion, the resolution consists of three sections. The first elaborates on the importance, urgency and overall requirements of persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. "Strengthening the Party spirit represents a fundamental task in our efforts to ensure full and rigorous Party self-governance," the resolution says. It also states that the implementation of democratic centralism is "an inherent requirement for exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance." On cultivating high-caliber officials capable of shouldering the mission of national rejuvenation, the resolution emphasizes that "strict management of officials is the key to full and rigorous governance over the Party". The resolution stresses the principal role of Party organizations at all levels in exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance and identifies improving conduct and tightening discipline as effective measures to advance this work. Hong Xianghua, a professor at the Party School of the Communist Party of China Central Committee (National Academy of Governance), said the resolution demonstrates the Party leadership's firm determination to persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance. He said its systematic arrangements would further strengthen the system of Party self-governance, ensuring comprehensive coverage and a complete chain of responsibility.

item.title: Could this be one of China's best places to do business?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
Could this be one of China's best places to do business? Share - WeChat
The 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit is set to take place in Wuzhen, Zhejiang province. Since 2014, this international event has called Zhejiang home. Why Zhejiang? In this episode of China Insight, we explore how this manufacturing powerhouse helps turn research into real-world applications, fosters collaboration among businesses, and nurtures emerging industries.
